_purpose: Records whose filing shows the adopted prior-year development figure to be a take-on: the reserves a loss portfolio transfer brought in, or an RITC premium. A take-on is not development. run_analysis.py (load_and_classify) tags such a record TAKEON_NOT_DEVELOPMENT when it would otherwise be reliable: the record stays in the corpus and is not modelled, the way a net-basis record is recorded and excluded, and the disposition ledger counts it in a step of its own. A syndicate-year in the RITC regime whose adopted figure is development stays in the sample. takeon_amount_m is the transferred amount the filing states, in millions of the report's own currency; where no filing states it, the readings' inference, marked so in takeon_amount_basis. The loader refuses an entry without two readings, its pages and a quote; an entry marked _to_complete is skipped, not applied, until it carries them. A triangle figure whose latest step the filing shows to be dominated by a take-on is a take-on in the same sense (1274/2018: the Motor RITC accepted on 1 January 2018), and so is the premium of a loss portfolio transfer adopted as development (1980/2018). A figure the filing shows to be dominated by the commutation of such a transfer back to its cedant is not development either (1856/2020, the mirror of 1856/2018's take-on; R221, the frozen review's M02: the same rule for analogous quota-share transfers); its takeon_amount_m is the amount the filing prints for the transfer out, with a negative sign.

Syndicate 1955 wrote off 47.8m of reinsurance assets for it (1955/2020, note 12). Both readings put the commutation at 76-79% of the -62.513m figure, all of it in the 2016 and 2017 columns

This reduced the gross written premium in the year to £79m.' p48: 'Further, the Syndicate refunded £49.1m as a result of commuting 2017 and prior years of account back to Syndicate 1955.' p38, gross claims development (£000), end-2019 to end-2020: 2016 95,099 / 45,248; 2017 92,909 / 77,603; 2018 99,934 / 102,578 (-62,513 in all). p33: at 1 January 2020 gross 184,673, no transfer row. Syndicate 1955's 2020 report (p4): 'The 2017 quota share contract with Syndicate 1856 was commuted on 1 January 2020 ... The Syndicate received a refund amounting to £49.1m from Syndicate 1856.'
readings: R221 found in passing, reader A (2026-09-21): error; the commutation dominates. It is an outward transfer of 1856's quota-share liabilities for 1955's 2017-and-prior years, effective 1 January 2020, not development of 1856's own reserves: about 47.8m (1955's reinsurance asset written off) to 49.1m (the refund), 76-79% of -62.513m, all in the 2016 and 2017 columns; re-estimation about -13.4m to -14.7m. The rules as written do not net out an outward transfer; by analogy with a dominating take-on, exclusion is the owner's decision.

R221 found in passing, reader B (2026-09-21): not development of 1856's own reserves. The commutation dominates the figure: it sends the whole-account quota-share liabilities for 2017 and prior back to the cedant, including 1955's 2015-and-prior reserves taken on in 2018; about -49.1m of the -62.5m (about 79%) if 1856 held them at the refund. The rules as written cover only inward take-ons; this is the mirror case.
